_README: Return values of the fused-memory submit_task tool and the typed outcome shared/src/shared/task_submit.py::parse_submit_task_result must classify each as. Read by orchestrator/tests/test_scheduler_submit_task.py, which wraps each 'payload' (the tool's own return value) in the production JSON-RPC body via orchestrator/tests/_orch_helpers.py::mcp_tool_envelope (a case with 'jsonrpc_result' instead carries the 'result' member verbatim, for FastMCP's prose isError form that has no dict payload) and asserts Scheduler.submit_task returns 'outcome'; and by fused-memory/tests/test_task_interceptor.py, which asserts the real TaskInterceptor.submit_task returns each case marked "live": true. Both readers pin one file, so a drift in either the server's response shape or the parser fails a test. Only the "live": true cases are asserted against the real server; the others pin parser behaviour on shapes the server can produce.
